title: AUTH-007 MFA Audit Event Binding

authority.actorRule: Actor and target identity are derived server-side from the authenticated W02 principal or the identity-bound W02 challenge; never accept caller-supplied actor, user ID, role, layer, or MFA assurance.

events.name: auth.mfa.enrollment_started
events.trigger: A valid authenticated enrollment attempt starts a pending factor.

events.name: auth.mfa.enrollment_verified
events.trigger: W02 confirms the pending TOTP factor and reads back enabled+verified state.

events.name: auth.mfa.enrollment_failed
events.trigger: An enrollment attempt fails after the identity has been authoritatively resolved.

events.name: auth.mfa.challenge_succeeded
events.trigger: A valid TOTP or recovery-code challenge is verified.

events.name: auth.mfa.challenge_failed
events.trigger: A challenge verification fails after its identity-bound subject is resolved.

events.name: auth.mfa.factor_disabled
events.trigger: A factor disable operation succeeds after password and TOTP step-up and session invalidation.

events.name: auth.mfa.recovery_codes_rotated
events.trigger: Recovery codes are rotated after password and TOTP step-up; plaintext codes are disclosed only through the permitted one-time response.

events.name: auth.mfa.recovery_code_consumed
events.trigger: A single-use recovery code is successfully consumed during challenge verification.

events.name: auth.mfa.locked
events.trigger: The authoritative provider/factor enters its locked state after bounded failures.

events.name: auth.mfa.replay_rejected
events.trigger: W02's persisted atomic TOTP time-step guard rejects a reused or concurrent duplicate time-step.

delivery.admissionRule: Do not claim event delivery or audit persistence until the exact existing W02-to-W06 transport, consumer behavior, idempotency, and failure semantics are tied to executable tests and current-head production evidence.

invariants: Successful factor or recovery mutations must have an immutable canonical audit record after the authoritative mutation is accepted.
Security failures are audited without logging factor secrets, TOTP/recovery codes, raw session tokens, challenge tokens, or secret-derived hashes.
Repeated delivery must be idempotent and must not create duplicate logical audit records.
W02 remains the only authority for factor state and TOTP replay decisions; W06 remains the canonical AuditEvent persistence authority.
Audit delivery failure must not be reported as successful evidence; the contract must define a fail-closed or admitted durable-outbox behavior before runtime acceptance.
verificationRequirements: All ten event names are registered and mapped to canonical AUTH-007 operations.
W02 producer source and the existing W02-to-W06 transport are verified against the exact commit SHA.
W06 consumes each event and persists canonical AuditEvent records without duplicate logical writes.
Positive and negative tests prove actor/target provenance, secret redaction, replay rejection, duplicate-delivery idempotency, and audit failure handling.
Current-head Evidence Registry records and Mapping 0 validation are required before AUTH-007 promotion.
nonGoals: Does not claim that runtime event emission is implemented.
Does not authorize D1 migration, Worker deployment, MFA rollout, or first-L8 grant.
Does not add a Worker, D1 database, Queue, or Service Binding.
